evidence.excerpt: Forty-eight zinc-oxide varistor discs rated 275 V rms, 6 kA (8/20 µs), were subjected to repetitive impulse stress to quantify degradation under conditions representative of indirect lightning exposure. Three stress protocols were used: 100 pulses at 1 kA, 50 pulses at 3 kA, and 20 pulses at 6 kA (all 8/20 µs). Varistor clamping voltage, leakage current at 0.9 times rated dc voltage, and thermal dissipation factor were measured before and after each protocol. Clamping voltage increased by 4–11% after 100 pulses at 1 kA and by 18–27% after 20 pulses at 6 kA. Leakage current increased by one order of magnitude in eight of sixteen specimens stressed at 6 kA, indicating incipient failure. Scanning electron microscopy of cross-sections revealed grain boundary degradation concentrated in a cylindrical core region. The results suggest that standard SPD replacement intervals based solely on visual inspection or power-frequency leakage tests are insufficient for sites with high indirect-lightning flash density above 2 flashes km⁻² yr⁻¹.
